item: Explicit quadratic latent alphabet gadget: block C_blk(x,y) = y + Q(x) with Q(x) = (x2x3, x1x3, x1x2) on F_{2^d}^3, update spaces U_A, oriented recursion, quotient and enlargement (lem:latent of The Unique Games Theorem)
item_type: F3 (auxiliary construction / gadget; witness-like object whose design could be reused)
method_note: Text-level only. The Lean was NOT compiled (no local toolchain, no local Mathlib checkout). Dependencies traced by reading imports and proofs and by grep over the whole OAI tree. WebSearch was unavailable for the whole session (account session limit); no web query returned results. Literature items below are from the analyst's own knowledge and from data/pilot/102/novelty.* and must be checked.
lean_status_why: Quadratic/Block.lean defines exactly Q, its polar D and the block spaces U_A of eq. (2.4)/(2.5), and Gadgets/ runs the same oriented recursion, harmonic-rank argument, quotient and enlargement to prove exists_actual_gadget, which is lem:latent (equivariance, change probability <= p, detection >= 1/8 above a rank threshold fixed before l) and which feeds theorem11 through exists_split_gadget.
lean_gaps: lem:latent also asserts that for rational p_* the threshold and finite data are produced by a terminating deterministic algorithm. exists_actual_gadget is purely existential (noncomputable section, Classical); the algorithmic clause is not formalized. theorem11 is unaffected because the gadget is fixed data for fixed errors.
Noise law: the paper uses a rational distribution mu; Lean uses the uniform law on a finite nonempty NoiseIndex with multiplicities. Equivalent.

Detection: the paper quantifies over subspaces G <= V* with dim(G|_K) >= r_* and asks Pr[exists g in G, g(a) != 0] >= 1/8; Lean quantifies over linear maps S with finrank(range(S . embed)) >= r and asks Pr[S(noise) = 0] <= 7/8. Equivalent reformulation.
Lean's rank threshold is explicit, r = finrank(B) + 2 = 3d + 2 for the chosen field size 2^d (Final.lean). The paper only asserts existence of r_*.
Comparator theorem11 matches thm:ugc (binary 3SAT, epsilon, delta in (0,1/2)) and is stronger in format: simple bipartite, unweighted, translation constraints, explicit TM2 polytime machine.

Section 7 consequences (Raghavendra, ordering CSPs, multicut and sparsest cut, Min-2CNF deletion, correlation clustering) are not Lean targets. The OptimalMaxCut and DirectedFeedback comparators DO depend on the gadget, but only through namespace-renamed full copies of the UG development (MaxCutGames.theorem11, DFVSGames.theorem11). That is a different route from the Max-Cut paper, which avoids the gadget and works from DKKMS 2-to-1 games plus Majority Is Stablest.
VertexCover and MinUncut do not depend on the gadget: no Q, no exists_actual_gadget and no theorem11 in those directories.

lean_source.name: OAI.UniqueGamesTheorem.Quadratic.Q
lean_source.text:
/-- The three-coordinate quadratic block from equation (2.4). -/
def Q (x : Vec F) : Vec F := ![x 1 * x 2, x 0 * x 2, x 0 * x 1]

lean_source.name: OAI.UniqueGamesTheorem.Quadratic.D
lean_source.text:
/-- Its polar cross-terms.  In characteristic two these equal
`Q (x + a) + Q x + Q a`. -/
def D (x a : Vec F) : Vec F :=
  ![x 1 * a 2 + a 1 * x 2, x 0 * a 2 + a 0 * x 2,
    x 0 * a 1 + a 0 * x 1]

lean_source.name: OAI.UniqueGamesTheorem.Quadratic.D_eq_polar
lean_source.text: theorem D_eq_polar (x a : Vec F) : D x a = Q (x + a) + Q x + Q a :=

lean_source.name: OAI.UniqueGamesTheorem.Quadratic.Q_add_of_mem_line
lean_source.text:
/-- The restriction of the quadratic map to one field line is additive. -/
theorem Q_add_of_mem_line (v a b : Vec F)
    (ha : a ∈ line v) (hb : b ∈ line v) : Q (a + b) = Q a + Q b :=

lean_source.name: OAI.UniqueGamesTheorem.Quadratic.U
lean_source.text:
/-- The block space `U_A`, as an actual binary submodule.  Membership uses
`y + Q a` because subtraction equals addition in characteristic two. -/
def U (v : Vec F) : Submodule (ZMod 2) (Vec F × Vec F) where
  carrier := {p | p.1 ∈ line v ∧ dot v (p.2 + Q p.1) = 0}

lean_source.name: OAI.UniqueGamesTheorem.Gadget.ActualGadget.Data
lean_source.text:
structure Data (C : Type) [AddCommGroup C] [Module F2 C] where
  Ambient : Type
  [ambientAddCommGroup : AddCommGroup Ambient]
  [ambientModule : Module F2 Ambient]
  [ambientFintype : Fintype Ambient]
  embed : C →ₗ[F2] Ambient
  embed_injective : Function.Injective embed
  f : Ambient → C
  equivariant : ∀ x c, f (x + embed c) = f x + c
  NoiseIndex : Type
  [noiseFintype : Fintype NoiseIndex]
  [noiseNonempty : Nonempty NoiseIndex]
  noise : NoiseIndex → Ambient

lean_source.name: OAI.UniqueGamesTheorem.Gadget.ActualGadget.Satisfies
lean_source.text:
/-- The stability and dispersion claim of Theorem 3.4 for fixed errors and rank. -/
def Satisfies (g : Data C) (ζ ν : ℚ) (r : Nat) : Prop :=
  stabilityError g ≤ ζ ∧
  ∀ (P : Type) [AddCommGroup P] [Module F2 P] (S : g.Ambient →ₗ[F2] P),
    r ≤ Module.finrank F2 (S.comp g.embed).range → kernelError g S ≤ ν

lean_source.name: OAI.UniqueGamesTheorem.Gadget.QuadraticStageNoise.actual_kernel
lean_source.text:
theorem actual_kernel (d : Vec F) (hd : d ≠ 0) :
    (𝔼 i : BlockOrientationIndex F, 𝔼 p : Vec F × Vec F,
      NonlinearRecurrence.change (fun z => z.2 + Q z.1) p (blockEmbedding i d)) =
      rate F :=

lean_source.name: OAI.UniqueGamesTheorem.Gadget.QuadraticStageNoise.stage_error
lean_source.text:
theorem stage_error (n : ℕ) :
    StageNoiseRecurrence.error (stage (F := F) n) =
      (1 - 1 / (Nat.card F : ℚ) ^ 3) * rate F ^ n :=

lean_source.name: OAI.UniqueGamesTheorem.Gadget.BaseConstruction.exists_base
lean_source.text:
/-- The unconditional finite base endpoint. All choices depend only on `p`;
the larger logical alphabet used by the final enlargement is absent here. -/
theorem exists_base (p : ℚ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    ∃ d : ℕ, 0 < d ∧ ∃ n : ℕ,
      StageNoiseRecurrence.error (quotientStage (F := BinaryField d) n) ≤ p ∧
      ∀ (E : Type) [AddCommGroup E] [Module (ZMod 2) E]
        (T : (quotientStage (F := BinaryField d) n).Input →ₗ[ZMod 2] E),
        Function.Injective (T.comp (quotientStage (F := BinaryField d) n).embed) →
        (1 / 4 : ℚ) ≤ StageNoiseRecurrence.average (fun t =>
          if T ((quotientStage (F := BinaryField d) n).noise t) ≠ 0 then 1 else 0) :=

lean_source.name: OAI.UniqueGamesTheorem.Gadget.exists_actual_gadget
lean_source.text:
/-- Actual finite gadget data, with a rank threshold independent of the final
logical dimension and an arbitrarily small nonlinear change probability. -/
theorem exists_actual_gadget (p : ℚ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    ∃ r : ℕ, 1 ≤ r ∧ ∀ ℓ : ℕ, r ≤ ℓ →
      ∃ g : UniqueGamesTheorem.Gadget.ActualGadget.Data (Vector ℓ),
        UniqueGamesTheorem.Gadget.ActualGadget.Satisfies g p (7 / 8) r :=

lean_source.name: OAI.UniqueGamesTheorem.Gadget.exists_split_gadget
lean_source.text:
theorem exists_split_gadget (p : ℚ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    ∃ r : ℕ, 1 ≤ r ∧ ∀ ℓ : ℕ, r ≤ ℓ →
      ∃ d : ℕ, ∃ g : UniqueGamesTheorem.Reduction.ActualSource.SplitGadget ℓ d,
        g.stabilityError ≤ p ∧
        ∀ (P : Type) [AddCommGroup P] [Module F2 P]
          (S : UniqueGamesTheorem.Reduction.ActualSource.Ambient ℓ d →ₗ[F2] P),
          r ≤ Module.finrank F2
            (S.comp (UniqueGamesTheorem.Reduction.ActualSource.alphabetEmbedding ℓ d)).range →
          UniqueGamesTheorem.Integration.SplitGadget.kernelProbability g S ≤ 7 / 8 :=

lean_source.name: OAI.UniqueGamesTheorem.theorem11
lean_source.text:
/-- For every fixed pair of errors in `(0, 1/2)`, binary 3SAT reduces in
polynomial time to translation Unique Games with completeness at least `1 - ε`
and soundness at most `δ`. The alphabet and machine depend only on the errors. -/
theorem theorem11 (ε δ : ℝ)
    (hε : 0 < ε) (hεhalf : ε < 1 / 2)
    (hδ : 0 < δ) (hδhalf : δ < 1 / 2) :
    Nonempty (Explicit.MachineOutputContract.BinaryGapReduction ε δ) :=

speedup_targets.title: Perfect completeness for 2-to-1 games (release family 105)
speedup_targets.statement: For every rational delta in (0,1) it is NP-hard to distinguish satisfiable 2-to-1 games from games of value <= delta, over a fixed alphabet (OAI.PerfectCompleteness.Theorem11.exists_reduction).
speedup_targets.reference: OpenAI release fd4aeeb, preprints/Perfect-completeness-for-2-to-1-games-September-23-2026; Lean OAI/Computability/PerfectCompleteness (581 files).
speedup_targets.status: claimed proved (unrefereed); Lean-formalized end to end in the release
speedup_targets.current_proof_size: Paper about 60+ pages (not counted precisely); Lean 581 files.
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: The two proofs share an architecture: a recursive tree whose spaces are spanned by products of child functions, explored along a random root-to-leaf path. The genericity and harmonic rank-loss lemmas in UniqueGames/Quadratic (GenericSeparationLemmas, HarmonicLoss, GenericSubspaceProbability) might replace parts of 105's rank-splitting decoders (Algebra/DecoderRankSplit, FunctionSpaceLowerRank). The Q block itself cannot be used as completeness noise, because perfect completeness forbids change probability p > 0 (see negative control N1).

lean_feasibility.formal_proof_to_compare: yes: run the 105 comparator with and without UniqueGames/Quadratic + Gadgets imported; Lean-vs-Lean size comparison is direct

speedup_targets.title: Near-perfect-completeness hardness with quadratic or low-degree codes (Khot-Saket 2014; Dinur-Guruswami 2013)
speedup_targets.statement: Khot-Saket (FOCS 2014): given a graph that is almost q-colorable (q-colorable after removing an epsilon fraction of vertices or edges), it is NP-hard to find an independent set of small relative size. Exact size bound not recalled; check against the paper. Dinur-Guruswami (FOCS 2013): PCPs via the low-degree long code, giving hardness for constrained hypergraph coloring.
speedup_targets.reference: S. Khot, R. Saket, 'Hardness of finding independent sets in almost q-colorable graphs', FOCS 2014 (arXiv 1408.0262 per novelty.json); I. Dinur, V. Guruswami, 'PCPs via the low-degree long code and hardness for constrained hypergraph coloring', FOCS 2013 / Israel J. Math 2015. Parameters quoted from memory, unverified.
speedup_targets.current_proof_size: about 30-40 pages each (from memory); no formalization known.
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: Both papers face the same obstruction as lem:latent: tests that are linear in the code lose completeness under translation noise, and quadratic or low-degree codes are used to recover completeness close to 1. The latent gadget is a different fix: the honest answer is nonlinear in the table, while any linear observation of high rank detects the noise. A gadget-based test could replace the low-degree-code completeness analysis. This is speculative; no concrete reduction was worked out.

speedup_targets.statement: For every epsilon, delta > 0 it is NP-hard to distinguish Max-3-Lin(F2) instances with value >= 1-epsilon from those with value <= 1/2 + delta.
speedup_targets.reference: J. Håstad, 'Some optimal inapproximability results', JACM 48 (2001).

One expects no gain, because Håstad's noise analysis is already short; the target is useful as a calibration point that should show no speedup.

speedup_verdict: No strong device-level speedup target found. Every known theorem that clearly gets shorter with the gadget available (Max-Cut at alpha_GW, Vertex Cover 2-epsilon, Raghavendra CSPs, DFVS, Min-UnCut, sparsest cut, kernel clustering, 2-to-2 games with completeness 1-epsilon) gets shorter through theorem11, so it is a corollary and does not count as device reuse. The release's own Lean is the strongest measurable evidence: for OptimalMaxCut and DirectedFeedback the formalizers chose the gadget/theorem11 route over the papers' direct routes, and vendored about 63k-66k lines of copied UG development each.

theorem_corollaries: Max-Cut NP-hard beyond alpha_GW (KKMO07 + MOO10). In Lean, OptimalMaxCut is proved via a vendored theorem11 copy; the Max-Cut paper proves it directly without the gadget.

Vertex Cover NP-hard below factor 2 (Khot-Regev 2008), paper sec. 7. The release proves VertexCover directly (66k Lean lines, no gadget). That gives a measurable with/without comparison at corollary level, if KR08 were formalized.
Raghavendra's optimal CSP thresholds (cor:raghavendra-consequence) and ordering CSPs (Guruswami-Håstad-Manokaran-Raghavendra-Charikar 2011).
Multicut, non-uniform sparsest cut, Min-2CNF-equivalence deletion, correlation clustering (CKKRS06; sec. 7).
DFVS constant-factor hardness (Svensson's UG reduction). In Lean, DirectedFeedback is proved via a vendored DFVSGames.theorem11 copy.
Uniform sparsest cut constant-factor hardness (family 117 paper uses the UG theorem as premise; its Lean comparator covers only the integrality gap).
Kernel clustering hardness (family 096; Lean covers only the propeller bound).
2-to-2 games with completeness 1-epsilon: immediate from UG by label doubling (KMS18 then becomes a corollary).
release_reuse: Full-tree grep: Q is defined in exactly three places in OAI: UniqueGames/Quadratic/Block.lean:20, MaxCut/Games/OrientationVectors.lean:95 and DirectedFeedback/Games/ChildLifts.lean:422. exists_actual_gadget / StableNonlinearDispersion appear only in those three trees.

MaxCut/Games (117 files, about 63k lines) and DirectedFeedback/Games (about 66k lines) are namespace-renamed copies of the UG development, consumed through theorem11. That is reuse of the theorem, not independent reuse of the design.

Family 105 (2-to-1 perfect completeness) shares the recursive product-tree architecture (quadraticSpan, dependentQuadraticSpan in Construction/FactoredFunctionsLemmas.lean) but not Q, U_A or the latent separation property. This looks like a house style; priority between the two is unknown.
The Max-Cut paper's 'latent resampling rows' (decoding.tex) are a different device (planted zero coefficients); only the name is shared.

negative_controls.title: N1 (proved-false analogue): latent gadget with p_* = 0
negative_controls.statement: There is no Data g over K = F_2^l with stabilityError g = 0 and kernelError <= nu < 1 for every S of restriction rank >= r, whenever l >= r.
negative_controls.why: If C(x+a) = C(x) for all a in supp(mu), let A = span(supp mu). Equivariance forces A ∩ K = 0. Then G = A^perp restricts onto all of K^*, so it has rank l >= r_*, yet it vanishes on every noise vector, so the detection probability is 0. Any gadget must therefore pay p > 0. This is why perfect-completeness results (105, approximate coloring under 2-to-1) cannot use it as completeness noise.

negative_controls.title: N2: Unique Games with perfect completeness, on expanders, or with entangled provers
negative_controls.statement: Satisfiable UG is in P (propagation / Gaussian elimination for translations); UG on spectral expanders is easy (Arora-Khot-Kolla-Steurer-Tulsiani-Vishnoi 2008); entangled-prover UG is in P (Kempe-Regev-Toner 2008).
negative_controls.why: Gadget-based reductions must yield imperfect completeness, non-expanding constraint graphs and classical-only soundness. Targets that need any of these three properties should show no speedup.

top5.target: Quantitative trade-off r_*(p_*) / UG alphabet size
top5.argument: This is the only target that tests the device itself rather than its theorem, and it needs no new definitions: Data and Satisfies already express it. An upper-bound improvement is a direct measure of how much the construction can be compressed. A lower bound, extending the proved-false p = 0 control, would show whether the gadget's parameters are forced. Both feed the alphabet and size of UG hardness.

This is a clean test of device generality. The Lean pins exactly which lemmas are characteristic-2 specific (D_eq_polar, cross_self_zero, D_smul_smul_zero). If a prover with Quadratic/ in its library finds an odd-characteristic analogue much faster than one without it, that is device reuse. The hardness consequence is already a corollary via KKMO, so the result has to be judged as a construction.

This is the only Lean-vs-Lean measurable device-level comparison. Run the 105 comparator with and without UniqueGames/Quadratic + Gadgets imported. Expectation is low: N1 forbids using the gadget as noise, but the genericity and harmonic lemmas may transfer. Even a null result calibrates the test.

These are the closest known theorems facing the same completeness-under-linear-structure obstruction, which they solve with quadratic or low-degree codes. A gadget-based reproof would be genuine device reuse. Confidence is low, and the PCP infrastructure (Label Cover, repetition) exists only inside the UG tree.

The payoff is very high, but the obstruction match is weak: the gadget does not touch the expansion of the constraint graph. Include it as a long shot and as a check on whether a prover over-generalises the device.
